title: PrimaDaNoi: right-to-be-forgotten removal demands and litigation over a news archive
exclusion_reason: Outside platform copyright/trademark abuse mandate; judicial RTBF and privacy litigation rather than platform notice-and-action takedown
summary: Italian local news site PrimaDaNoi received some 240 legal demands over a decade to remove archived articles on privacy and right-to-be-forgotten grounds, about 40 of which reached court; the demands were addressed to the publisher, not to Google. Held liable over a 2008 report on a restaurant stabbing, its editor accumulated at least €50,000 in legal costs and fines, and the site suspended publication in September 2018. In Biancardi v. Italy (2021) the ECtHR unanimously found no violation of Article 10.

title: Complaint campaign against Uzbek independent journalists' and activists' accounts
exclusion_reason: Mostly personal accounts of individual journalists and activists rather than institutional newsroom assets; the outlet-level episodes involving AsiaTerra are coded in cases.csv (ASIATERRA-001, ASIATERRA-002)
summary: From early 2026, accounts and pages of Uzbek independent journalists and activists on Facebook, Instagram, YouTube and Telegram were removed or blocked after waves of complaints, mostly alleging copyright infringement; some were filed from fake profiles and e-mail addresses impersonating journalists. Affected accounts include those of Farida Sharifullina (restored after numerous appeals), Shukhrat Babajanov (restored after a month with the help of an international organisation), Ulugbek Khaydarov (suspended on 30 March 2026 after a complaint filed in the name of the UzA news agency) and Abdurakhmon Tashanov.

title: AiPlex copyright strike on Respublika Telegram posts
exclusion_reason: Telegram platform excluded from core DSA VLOP / notice-and-action dataset analysis
summary: On 22 May 2025 Telegram notified Respublika.kz.media of a copyright complaint from 'Aiplex' and removed two posts of 17 May about the refusal of entry to Russia of journalists Irina Mednikova and Lukpan Akhmedyarov; a comment under one of the posts was removed later. The newsroom received no reply from the address given in the notice.

title: AiPlex false copyright claims against K-pop music videos on YouTube
exclusion_reason: Non-journalistic target context; preserved solely as evidentiary benchmark of vendor industrial automated error rates and platform awareness
summary: On 15 January 2019 YouTube removed official music videos by BLACKPINK, BTS member V, PSY, BigBang and Twice after copyright claims filed by AiPlex Software; the videos were restored within hours. Smaller channels had reported false claims from AiPlex since 2017, and a petition asking YouTube to ban AiPlex gathered nearly 8,000 signatures.

title: Deletion of Vadim Boreyko's personal social media accounts
exclusion_reason: Personal accounts of an individual journalist; no platform notice or legal basis has been documented
summary: The Facebook page of Kazakhstani journalist Vadim Boreyko, author of the Giperborey channel, was deleted in July 2025, after the earlier loss of a backup Facebook channel and of his TikTok account in 2024. No platform notice or stated ground has been published; Boreyko describes the deletions as targeted attacks.

title: Copyright complaints to Google against Maltese websites covering the state hospitals privatisation deal
exclusion_reason: Senders not identified (complaints filed under different names or pseudonyms), and individual target outlets, notices and outcomes are not documented case by case; kept as European-target context alongside Part 3.3 of the report
summary: In May 2024 Times of Malta reported that scores of copyright complaints targeting Maltese websites were filed with Google from March 2024, weeks before a magisterial inquiry into the privatisation of three state hospitals concluded; in April 2024 former Prime Minister Joseph Muscat and two other former senior officials were charged in connection with the deal. Megan Mallia, a University of Malta researcher writing for EDMO/MedDMO (January 2025), found that one blog post alone received at least five complaints, each filed under a different name or pseudonym in close succession and each claiming that the post had copied a different article. Searches combining Maltese news sites and blogs with "ram tumuluri" or "vitals global healthcare" (September 2024) returned Google notices that results had been removed following copyright complaints. Who filed the complaints has not been established.
